question: Explain how hash table collisions are handled.
answer: Different keys may map to the same bucket. Chaining keeps entries in a bucket and compares full keys; open addressing probes other slots. With a good hash and controlled load, expected operations are constant time, but worst-case lookup can be linear. Resize as load grows and test duplicate keys and adversarial collisions.
